edition.alertText: Oil rebounds 2.3% — Brent settles ~$91.40 as fresh Hormuz attacks reverse Monday's 3-month low; Iran Navy says 2 more tankers caught fire from mines east of Hormuz on Tuesday; IRGC claims container ship hit mine on 'unauthorized' route near Hormuz on Wednesday — first container vessel targeted; Houthi drone strikes PIF tower in Riyadh for second time in a week — 11 injured including 2 Indians (Saudi Civil Defence); Saudi coalition issues evacuation warning for Hodeidah port — Houthis threaten to target Jeddah and all Saudi Red Sea ports; Trump gives Iran until early 2027 to strike deal — warns strikes could resume; calls Iranian negotiators 'professional tap dancers'; US Treasury sanctions dozens in new Iran shadow banking crackdown; WSJ: US investigating Iranian cyberattacks on ~50 ships; Iran Navy declares Hormuz 'will never be reopened' until 7 conditions met; Hormuz Strait Monitor: only 2 vessels passed in 24 hours vs ~60 average — traffic at ~3% of normal; Windward: 8 AIS-dark crossings Nov 20-23; Houthi-run media: Saudi strikes on buses in Lahj kill 25; Saudi coalition airstrikes on Sanaa airport positions; gold falls 2% to ~$3,562 as precious metals rout deepens — down from $3,635 rebound; Deutsche Bank: global oil surplus 1.7M b/d in October; Eni CEO: Hormuz shipping surcharge ~$25-30/bbl; OPEC+ meets Nov 29 on 2027 output — IEA surplus complicates expansion; Iran judiciary claims $290B in court-awarded damages against US

situation: Oil rebounded sharply on Tuesday after Monday's crash to three-month lows, as fresh attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz reminded markets that the geopolitical risk premium cannot be fully unwound while Iran's mine and missile campaign continues. Brent settled at approximately $91.40/bbl, up $2.03 (+2.27%), while WTI recovered to approximately $82.05/bbl (+2.35%), after both benchmarks had touched their lowest levels since late August during Monday's session — Brent briefly fell to $88.10 and WTI to $79.07. Iran's navy reported that two more oil tankers caught fire after striking naval mines east of the Strait on Tuesday morning, while the IRGC said three tankers had exploded overnight on an 'unauthorized' route. On Wednesday, the IRGC claimed a container ship — the first non-tanker vessel type explicitly targeted — hit a mine on an 'unauthorized' route near the Strait, escalating the campaign to commercial shipping more broadly. The Hormuz Strait Monitor recorded only two vessel transits in the prior 24 hours versus a normal average of roughly 60, with traffic at approximately 3% of normal levels and around 400 ships waiting outside the Strait. Deutsche Bank estimated a global oil surplus of 1.7 million barrels per day in October based on rising observed stocks, and Eni CEO Claudio Descalzi said Hormuz shipping now carries a surcharge of approximately $25-30 per barrel on freight, taxes and insurance. Gold continued its steep decline, falling approximately 2% on Tuesday to around $3,562/oz after Monday's rebound to $3,635 had proved short-lived, as the precious metals rout deepened amid elevated Fed rate hike expectations — markets are pricing roughly 95% odds of a 25bp hike in December.

The diplomatic picture hardened as Trump gave Iran until early 2027 to reach a deal before military strikes could resume. In a Fox News interview on Sunday, Trump called Iranian negotiators 'professional tap dancers' and warned that vessels challenging the US naval blockade would be sent 'to the bottom of the sea.' Iran's navy responded by declaring the Strait 'will never be reopened' until all seven conditions are met — including ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing assets, lifting sanctions, oil export exemptions, and ending the naval blockade. Iran's deputy foreign minister Gharibabadi confirmed talks were continuing with Qatari mediators, while a Doha proposal from early November remains under consideration by both sides. Secretary of State Rubio met Qatar's PM in Washington on Monday as part of the biannual US-Qatar Strategic Dialogue, reaffirming US commitment to Qatar's security. The US Treasury announced new sanctions targeting dozens of individuals and entities in Iran's shadow banking network as part of Operation Economic Outcast, while the Wall Street Journal reported the US is investigating possible Iranian involvement in cyberattacks on approximately 50 oil, chemical and gas tankers — some receiving threatening messages — with Iran the primary suspect. Iran's judiciary claimed courts had awarded $290 billion in damages against the United States, with state media saying some US-linked commercial ships had been seized as partial compensation. Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf said there would be no negotiations until the seven conditions are met and warned Iran is ready to 'alter the geography of the battlefield.'

The Yemen conflict escalated dramatically as Houthi forces struck the PIF tower — Saudi Arabia's tallest skyscraper and sovereign wealth fund headquarters — for the second time in under a week on Tuesday, injuring 11 people including two Indian nationals according to Saudi Civil Defence. The Saudi-led coalition condemned the attack as 'cowardly terrorism' and issued an evacuation warning for Yemen's Hodeidah port, signaling a potential major operation against the Houthi-held Red Sea gateway. The Houthis responded by threatening to target Jeddah and all other Saudi Red Sea ports if Hodeidah is attacked, raising the specter of a second maritime chokepoint crisis at Bab al-Mandeb. Houthi-run Saba reported that Saudi F-15SA jets struck buses and commercial vehicles in Wadi Ma'baq, Lahj governorate, on November 23, killing 25 or more and wounding 6 — though government-aligned sources gave a lower toll of 6 dead. Saudi coalition airstrikes also targeted Houthi positions around Sanaa airport and in Dhamar. UKMTO confirmed three ships were struck by unidentified projectiles on November 23 while sailing east through the Strait, with all crews accounted for. Windward satellite tracking recorded eight AIS-dark crossings between November 20 and 23 — six inbound, two outbound — indicating continued covert transits. Iran braces for winter energy shortages with power cuts already in effect. The OPEC+ meeting on November 29 looms as a critical test: the IEA's declaration of the first supply surplus since the war began complicates any plans for 2027 output expansion, while ongoing attacks ensure the risk premium cannot fully dissipate.

Pentagon: war cost exceeds $48B; IRGC claims container ship hit mine on Nov 25 — first non-tanker targeted; Iran Navy: 2 more tankers caught fire from mines east of Hormuz on Nov 24; WSJ: US investigating Iranian cyberattacks on ~50 ships

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices eased from June-July peaks of $1,100-1,300/tonne to $740-890/tonne by mid-October (Kpler), but remain above pre-war avg of ~$500/tonne (CRU). ADNOC sees sulfur output doubling from 7M to 14-20M tonnes by 2030-2035 — CEO Al Jaberi calls sulfur 'the future gold' (Nov 18). ADNOC's Oct official selling price cut $70 to $890/tonne. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for eighth consecutive month — March through late November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva at COP31 (Nov 14) warned 45 million people could face severe food insecurity — urged US and Iran to immediately allow ~5 fertilizer vessels/day through Hormuz within 7-10 days. Fertilizer prices up ~30% since blockades began (UN). WHO: Yemen death toll since August escalation reaches 2,260, with 10,519 wounded; more than 1,600 dead and 300,000+ displaced since July (UN); UNICEF: 330,000+ displaced including 174,000 children. Sudan food prices doubled in 6 months; Nepal farmers cannot afford fertiliser. Countries facing significant impact: Mozambique, Kenya, Sudan, Somalia, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka. Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Middle East fertiliser exports declined by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies (The National).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Poland's Orlen becomes first buyer to terminate QatarEnergy LNG contract (1M tonnes/yr, oil-linked, through 2034) citing ongoing force majeure (S&P Global Platts, Nov 11). DES NW Europe LNG benchmark at $27.59/MMBtu on Nov 11, up 175% YoY. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). 31 laden LNG tankers exited Hormuz in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~€89.59/MWh (~$100.85); EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). Natural gas futures fell 8.2% to $3.13/MMBtu (Nov 23). IRGC claims gas carrier exploded after mine strike in eastern Hormuz (Nov 13). Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. EIA projects US heating oil households to pay $2,977 this winter — up 70.2% from last year. IMF projects 2026 GDP contractions: Kuwait and Iraq ~16%, Qatar ~15%. LNG flows at 40-45% of prewar levels. Iran braces for winter natural gas shortages — imposes power cuts as energy crisis deepens (Nov 23).

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B. Allianz Trade estimates >$200B in physical damage across GCC — 80+ energy facilities struck, a third severely damaged; cumulative economic losses projected at $790B through 2030. Arabian Gulf crude shipments fell 27.6% YoY to 531.3M tonnes in Jan-Oct 2026 — Gulf share of global seaborne crude fell from 39.8% to 30.6% (Banchero Costa/LSEG).
